A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CAMDP research work. The complete main texts, Appendices A–G, equations and diagrams are readable and support comparison despite substantial theoretical revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports algorithms, mathematical guarantees and analytic lower-bound constructions. Neither the main text nor the appendices report original empirical results.

after.justification: V2 remains entirely theoretical. Its expanded concentration proofs, linear-program calculations and hard-instance constructions are not experimental, simulation or data-analysis results.

M1.justification: Although v1 mentions discounted reductions, Algorithm 1 and its reference optimization use average-reward/Blackwell-optimal updates. V2 explicitly uses statewise discounted-optimal policies and normalized discounted constraint values in the dual update. Sections 4–5 also substantially revise the discount, perturbation, threshold and optimization parameter schedules; mixture output itself already existed in v1.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or tasks for empirical training or evaluation. Revisions to mathematical hard-instance families belong to the theoretical analysis.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods against the proposed algorithm. Cited algorithms provide theoretical context or proof ingredients, not experimental baselines.

E3.justification: Neither version contains an experimental evaluation protocol. The new balanced-sampling restriction concerns the lower-bound theorem, rather than a changed experimental procedure.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, empirical robustness tests, sensitivity experiments or case studies. The expanded appendices contain mathematical proofs.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, empirical uncertainty intervals or significance tests. Changes to concentration inequalities and theorem success probabilities are theoretical revisions.

E6.justification: Neither version contains empirical result entries, measured performance or experimental rankings. Revised sample-complexity guarantees and analytic optimization values are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: V2 changes the benchmark to external mixtures, introduces the policy-wise discounted variance assumption, and develops a new cross-signal concentration theorem with row-independent candidates and a Bernstein hierarchy. It revises primal–dual and sensitivity proofs and removes v1's bias-span/transient-time estimation lemmas. Appendices F–G rebuild the lower bounds using exact occupancy separations, balanced-sampling and adaptive testing arguments, and an actual H = Θ(D) calibration instead of relying only on H ≤ D.

C1.justification: V1 advertises general minimax-optimal CAMDP guarantees. V2's abstract and conclusion qualify the upper bounds by a variance condition and an external-mixture benchmark, and restrict the full B+H lower bound to balanced algorithms while retaining an adaptive H-scale lower bound. Cross-signal concentration also becomes an explicit main contribution.

C2.justification: V2 materially narrows the stated applicability of the results and explains why concentration covers the finite oracle-policy family rather than the entire policy class. It also distinguishes adaptive from balanced lower bounds and explains their worst-case combination. These replace v1's broader interpretation that the general minimax complexity had been resolved without those qualifications.

D1.justification: V2 specifies external-mixture execution, lexicographic oracle selection, grid and rounding conventions, and the distinction between n samples per transition row and Ntot = SAn. It explicitly requires supplied structural bounds and a positive Slater lower bound, replacing v1's suggestion that an estimated Slater constant could be used. Neither version supplies code or implementation benchmarks.

R1.justification: The related-work framework centered on Vaswani et al. (2022) and Zurek and Chen (2024) remains. V2 adds Li et al. (2020) for concentration analysis and removes references including Bartlett and Tewari, Paternain et al., and Wang et al. (2022). Its concluding novelty statement is qualified to balanced B+H rates and adaptive H-scale lower bounds.

P1.justification: The abstract, problem formulation, methodology, proof sketches and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The appendices replace substantial prose and reorganize the lower-bound arguments into explicit construction, separation, testing and calibration subsections. This is a broad expository revision beyond adding new theorems.

P2.justification: The existing diagram artwork is retained. V1's Figures 1–2 are combined into v2's Figure 1, and appendix Figures 5–6 become Figure 4; the six-state diagram is retained with new numbering and placement. Captions, figure sizing and the algorithm box change, while the overall visual template remains.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially improves the coherence and checkability of the central theory. Its discounted formulation and new Appendix D remove reliance on v1's empirical-span estimation argument, whose stated and derived sample bounds disagree; Appendices F–G add exact occupancy separations and explicit testing reductions. The guarantees are less general—external-mixture benchmarks, a variance assumption, and balanced sampling for the full lower bound—but stating these limits addresses material overclaiming in v1.
